messages:
beth_cs: Heads-up — Enterprise customer (AcmeEU) reporting intermittent 403s and spikes in request latency this morning. They gave a request_id: acme-req-20260317-7f2a. Happening around 09:12-09:18 UTC. Can SRE/eng help pull server-side logs and advise on repro steps?

alex_support: Thanks Beth. Can you confirm the exact timestamp and region? Also, do they have a curl they used or an SDK call we can mirror?

beth_cs: Region eu-west-1, approximate window 2026-03-17T09:12:30Z -> 2026-03-17T09:18:10Z. They only gave the request_id and a customer-side trace header: x-cust-trace: 0x4a3b. No curl yet.

devon_eng: I'll start a log hunt. Try this Kibana/KQL snippet (set time range +/- 5m):
```
request_id : "acme-req-20260317-7f2a" OR trace_id : "0x4a3b"
| sort @timestamp desc
```
If nothing shows up in hot indices, we may need to hit cold/archived shards.

maria_sre: Note on retention: hot (fast) indices = 30 days, cold (slower, searchable) indices = 90 days. If the event got routed to an archived tier we need an export request — let me know if KQL returns nothing. Also check the edge logs for authorization middleware.

alex_support: Devon — when you run the KQL, can you also search for upstream 502/503 around that req id? Customer saw both 403 and timeouts.

devon_eng: Ran the query against logs-prod-*/apiserver and found 3 lines referencing that request_id in eu-west-1-proxy between 09:12:31 and 09:12:45. Posting the trimmed log lines (sanitized):
```
[09:12:31Z] proxy: req_id=acme-req-20260317-7f2a client_ip=52.31.12.9 status=403 auth_policy=token-expired
[09:12:33Z] proxy: req_id=acme-req-20260317-7f2a upstream_latency_ms=1200 upstream_status=504
[09:12:45Z] proxy: req_id=acme-req-20260317-7f2a routed_to=node-gpu-12 kernel_q=high
```
Looks like the token was rejected first, then an upstream timeout.

beth_cs: Customer insists they used a fresh API key, but I'll ask for the SDK/curl they used and if they rotated keys earlier.

ryan_runtime: Could be KV cache/backpressure causing 504s if route hit a busy node. Devon — can you check node-gpu-12's recent CPU/GPU scheduling and queue length? I can also spin a canary route for them.

devon_eng: Will check metrics. In the meantime, request the customer to run a minimal curl with the following so we get a reproducible trace header:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>"
     -H "X-Request-Id: acme-local-<rand>"
     -H "X-Debug: 1"
     -d '{"inputs":"test"}'
     https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
Tell them to paste the response headers and the exact body. Also ask them to set a custom trace header (X-Cust-Trace) matching what they saw.

alex_support: I'll send that curl snippet and ask them to include the full response headers and a HAR if possible. Also requesting the customer to produce a debug bundle from their side (instructions below).

beth_cs: Sent the curl + HAR request. They replied with a HAR but redacted keys. HAR shows several 403 responses then one 504. Attached snippet (sanitized).

maria_sre: For server-side lookups beyond what Kibana shows, run this ES query against logs-cold-*/_search with routing by region:
```
POST /logs-cold-*/_search
{
  "query": {
    "bool": {
      "should": [
        {"match": {"request_id": "acme-req-20260317-7f2a"}},
        {"match": {"trace_id": "0x4a3b"}}
      ]
    }
  },
  "sort": [{"@timestamp": {"order": "desc"}}]
}
```
If that returns nothing, open a ticket to infra-archive with the index time and we can request a cold tier restore (24-48h).

devon_eng: Checked node-gpu-12: queue depth spiked ~09:12:32, GPU utilization at 98% for a 30s window, and a small GC event on the process (oom-killer false positive). Likely the 504s are capacity-related. 403 earlier suggests token validation failure pre-routing — maybe a mis-synced key or clock skew.

beth_cs: Customer replied — they rotated keys at 09:10 UTC and said they retried immediately. I'll ask them exact rotate steps and when the new key was deployed to their service.

alex_support: Next steps summary: 1) Beth to get customer's curl/har and key-rotation timestamps. 2) Devon to open infra ticket for node-gpu-12 incident and KV cache/backoff check. 3) Maria to kick cold-tier search if Kibana misses logs. 4) Ask customer to run the curl with X-Debug to get server-side trace headers.

logbot: audit: export-request queued (if needed) — ticket #ARCH-2879 created to restore logs for 2026-03-17 09:10-09:20 UTC in eu-west-1.

beth_cs: Thanks everyone. I'll loop back once I have the curl/HAR and key rotation times. :thumbsup:

alex_support: If customer shares the replayable curl response (with a redacted key), we can also attempt an internal replay in a safe sandbox to reproduce the 504s.

ryan_runtime: I'll pre-warm a small canary pool in eu-west-1 for them while this is investigated — should reduce impact if it's capacity-related.

beth_cs: Filed checklist with customer and asked for permission to forward debug bundle. They granted it; uploading bundle to secure link and will paste once available.
